broken.what: S18's wrong answer ('emergency aid is like for schools') was never corrected. The tutor jumped straight to Fairtrade, so the student keeps the misconception that emergency aid is long-term development aid.
The student asked a clarifying question ('what do you mean by very little'). It was ignored and the LIC question was dropped. Low income countries were never actually explained.

The tutor asked for colonialism's effect, then got an off-topic reply. It then said 'loses its factories and industries like that' as if it had already taught that colonialism destroyed industries, but it never had. This is a non-sequitur.
The tutor gave the answer, then immediately asked the same question back: Fairtrade money goes to schools and water, then 'Where does that extra Fairtrade money actually go?'
The student said 'nah not really' to more strategies. The tutor carried on anyway and re-asked a question the student had already answered at S21 (what debt-relief money is spent on).
SDGs were asked about before being taught, and intermediate technology got a one-line mention. Both were then marked as covered in the notes.
The extreme poverty threshold is inconsistent: '$2' in T26, then '$2.15' in T27. The same 1990 question was asked twice.
The student guessed 'half'. The tutor neither confirmed nor corrected this, and later said about 36% without saying the guess was too high.
'Development categories and the Brandt Line' was marked covered (2/5), but the Brandt Line was never mentioned in the chat. HDI was not taught either.
The tutor told the student 'you've got the right idea' for 'divided by countries', which was wrong.

fixes.change: Render markdown bold (**x**) as <strong> instead of showing literal asterisks.
Before moving on, explicitly correct any wrong answer (e.g. S18 emergency aid, S28 'half', S1 'countries'). Never re-ask a question just answered or just explained.

fixes.change: Answer clarifying questions (S8) before continuing. When the student says 'no' or asks to skip, give a 2–3 line summary and move to the next key point instead of asking another question.
Only mark a key point covered when its required terms were actually taught (Brandt Line, HDI, LIC for point 2; SDGs for point 4). Use one consistent figure: $2.15/day.
Hide or shorten the site title on phone (logo only) and truncate the breadcrumb pill with an ellipsis, so the header fits on one line without clipping.

T2: No problem! So life expectancy is just the average age people live to in a country — it tells us a lot about healthcare, food, clean water, all that stuff. If Japan's life expectancy is 84 but Sierra Leone's is 55, what does that big difference suggest about those two countries?

T10: So those income categories help us understand where countries sit right now, but some countries are changing fast.
